reasoning_trace.value: The paper discusses an enhanced asymmetrically clipped direct-current-biased optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (EADO-OFDM) scheme for flexible waveform design and resource allocation in optical wireless integrated sensing and communication (OW-ISAC). The system framework is illustrated in Fig. 1, and the signal processing procedures are shown in Fig. 2.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The EADO-OFDM scheme is proposed for OW-ISAC, which can adaptively assign part of the odd subcarriers to DCO-OFDM. The system framework is based on a LiDAR that can transmit and receive optical signals simultaneously, and the signal processing techniques are discussed for both communication and sensing.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper provides a detailed analysis of the signal model and signal processing techniques for EADO-OFDM, including the modeling of clipping noise and the derivation of expressions for SNDR on each subcarrier. The physical consistency of the reported metrics is validated through numerical simulations.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper solves the problem of flexible waveform design and resource allocation for OW-ISAC, but the remaining open challenges include the optimization of system parameters and the improvement of sensing precision in the presence of atmospheric turbulence.
